classification.difficultyReason: Identify the indicated right triangle and halve the appropriate base using the equal-side markings before finding its height.

content.prompt: Find the height of these triangles. Round your answer to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Upright equilateral triangle; all three sides have matching ticks. The left side is labelled 16 cm. A dashed altitude meets the base at a marked right angle.
spec.mathematics: The altitude bisects the 16 cm base, giving a right triangle with hypotenuse 16 cm and shorter known side 8 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: No height value or half-base value is shown.

answer.worked:
The altitude bisects the base, so half the base is $16\div2=8\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{16^2-8^2}\\h&=\sqrt{192}\\h&\approx13.9\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Wide upright isosceles triangle with matching ticks on its sloping sides. The left side is labelled 2.9 m and the base 4.3 m. A dashed vertical altitude has a right-angle marker at its foot.
spec.mathematics: The altitude bisects the 4.3 m base. The relevant right triangle has hypotenuse 2.9 m and base 2.15 m.
spec.answerVisibility: No height value or half-base value is shown.

answer.worked:
The altitude bisects the base, so half the base is $4.3\div2=2.15\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{2.9^2-2.15^2}\\h&=\sqrt{3.7875}\\h&\approx1.9\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rotated equilateral triangle with matching ticks on all sides and 85 mm beneath its lower sloping side. A dashed altitude runs from the lower-left vertex to the opposite side, ending at a right-angle marker.
spec.mathematics: The indicated altitude bisects the opposite 85 mm side, yielding a right triangle with hypotenuse 85 mm and known shorter side 42.5 mm.
spec.answerVisibility: No height value or half-side value is shown.

answer.worked:
The altitude bisects the opposite side, so half that side is $85\div2=42.5\text{ mm}$.
$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{85^2-42.5^2}\\h&=\sqrt{5418.75}\\h&\approx73.6\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Isosceles triangle pointing right. Its left vertical base is labelled 1.84 m and its lower sloping side 2.2 m. Matching ticks mark the sloping sides. A dashed horizontal altitude meets the left base at a right angle.
spec.mathematics: The altitude bisects the vertical base, producing a right triangle with hypotenuse 2.2 m and known shorter side 0.92 m.
spec.answerVisibility: No height value or half-base value is shown.

answer.worked:
The altitude bisects the base, so half the base is $1.84\div2=0.92\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{2.2^2-0.92^2}\\h&=\sqrt{3.9936}\\h&\approx2.0\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

spec.answerVisibility: No height value or half-base value is shown.

$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{35^2-9^2}\\h&=\sqrt{1144}\\h&\approx33.8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
